content: 1. If you experience swollen lymph nodes, shortness of breath, swelling in your feet, ankles, or legs, or notice dark-colored urine, contact your healthcare provider immediately. Additionally, if your skin or the whites of your eyes turn yellow (a condition known as jaundice), seek medical attention promptly. 2. Lupus is an autoimmune disorder in which your immune system attacks your own cells and organs. Certain medications, such as lansoprazole, can either cause drug-induced lupus or worsen pre-existing lupus. Notify your healthcare provider immediately if you develop new or worsening joint pain or a rash on your arms or cheeks. 3. Lansoprazole can reduce the absorption of vitamin B-12, potentially leading to a deficiency, especially if taken for three years or longer. Symptoms of vitamin B-12 deficiency include a sore tongue, weakness, or tingling and numbness in your hands or feet. If you experience these symptoms, stop taking lansoprazole and contact your healthcare provider. 4. Lansoprazole can cause low magnesium levels (hypomagnesemia), which can lead to serious complications such as seizures or heart rhythm problems. Those at higher risk include individuals taking lansoprazole for a long time or in combination with other medications that lower magnesium. Symptoms of hypomagnesemia include changes in heart rate or rhythm (e.g., fast or skipping heartbeat), dizziness, muscle spasms, or seizures. If you experience any of these, stop taking lansoprazole and contact your healthcare provider immediately. 5. Prolonged use of lansoprazole, especially in older adults or at high doses, may lead to bone loss and an increased risk of fractures. Discuss your risk with your healthcare provider if you are concerned. 6. Lansoprazole can cause severe allergic reactions. Stop using the medication and seek emergency medical help if you experience symptoms such as difficulty breathing or wheezing, a racing heart, fever, swollen lymph nodes, swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat, trouble swallowing, throat tightness, itching, skin rash, hives, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, lightheadedness, fainting, stomach cramps, or joint pain. 7. People allergic to lansoprazole, any proton pump inhibitor (PPI), or any ingredients in the specific product should not use lansoprazole. Your pharmacist can provide a list of ingredients in the product. 8. Lansoprazole may interact with other medications. Inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are taking. Specific medications to discuss include methotrexate, digoxin, warfarin, theophylline, clarithromycin, tacrolimus, certain antiretroviral medications (e.g., rilpivirine, nelfinavir, saquinavir), St. John’s Wort, and rifampin. 9. Do not take lansoprazole unless prescribed by a healthcare provider. Take it exactly as directed and do not share it with others, even if they have the same condition. Keep it out of reach of children. 10. Lansoprazole should be taken before meals. If you are also taking sucralfate, take lansoprazole at least 30 minutes before sucralfate. Do not chew, cut, or crush lansoprazole capsules. If you have trouble swallowing the capsule, you may open it and sprinkle the contents on one tablespoon of applesauce, cottage cheese, yogurt, or strained pears. Swallow the mixture immediately without mixing it with other foods. 11. Lansoprazole is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn. It may take 1 to 4 days for the medication to take full effect. 12. If you miss a dose of lansoprazole, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. 13. Lansoprazole may cause common side effects such as diarrhea, stomach pain, nausea, or constipation. If these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. 14. Serious side effects of lansoprazole include kidney problems (e.g., acute tubulointerstitial nephritis), antibiotic-associated diarrhea caused by Clostridioides difficile (C. diff), severe skin reactions (e.g., Stevens-Johnson Syndrome or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis), and a severe allergic reaction called DRESS (Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms). If you experience symptoms such as decreased urine output, blood in your urine, watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in your stool, severe stomach cramps, fever, painful red or purple skin that peels, or a rash, stop taking lansoprazole and seek medical attention immediately. 15. Lansoprazole may affect pregnancy or breastfeeding. Inform your healthcare provider if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Lansoprazole can pass into breast milk, so it is not recommended during breastfeeding. 16. If you or someone else has taken too much lansoprazole, seek medical help immediately by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222.
